## DETAILS

### Scope and existing implementation

- This step ports the existing point contract to the remote protocol and GacJS, makes the existing Touching demonstration work through those renderers, and updates/distributes its documentation. The broader plan's tutorial addition, other native platform providers, gesture recognition, control scrolling/selection behavior, and mobile text-input integration are outside this request.
- Step 1 already implements `NativePointInputState` and the acquisition helpers in `<GacUI repo>/Source/NativeWindow/GuiNativeWindow.h/.cpp`, composition routing in `<GacUI repo>/Source/Application/GraphicsHost/GuiGraphicsHost.cpp`, and hosted routing in `<GacUI repo>/Source/PlatformProviders/Hosted/GuiHostedController.cpp`. Reuse these contracts, including the existing point capture/release helpers, sparse contact slots, and deferred target removal. Do not add another public point API or attempt to make synchronous deletion inside an input handler safe.
- The whole-surface ownership requirement above supersedes the broader plan's proposal to negotiate renderer ownership with Core. A remote native renderer accepts the native sequence immediately; GacJS owns touch input over its renderer surface before contact begins. Core alone queries the application and decides between composition point delivery and mouse fallback. There is no acceptance round trip, per-control browser ownership setting, or mid-sequence switch to OS/browser fallback.
- WASM shares the intended browser point contract. Keep the shared renderer and protocol changes usable through the existing worker transport, but leave WASM-specific implementation, rebuilding, deployment, and runtime verification to the follow-up identified above. Describing the support contract does not constitute a record of a completed runtime test.

### Wire schema and ordering

- Extend `<GacUI repo>/Source/PlatformProviders/Remote/Protocol/Protocol_IO.txt` with explicit Started, Down/Update/Up/Enter/Leave, and End records. Started carries the first sample and precedes a separate first Down; End carries the completion timestamp and reason. Preserve every sample field and optional-value distinction from `NativeWindowPointInfo`, including modifiers, primary status, contact bounds, pressure, orientation, and platform frame identity.
- Keep four identities separate: the renderer connection, the renderer's sequence ID, the contact's Down-order `pointId`, and a per-sequence transport `eventIndex`. Timestamps and platform frame IDs do not establish event order. Started establishes index 0; actions and End consume successive indices beginning at 1, across all contacts in the sequence. A later contact does not reset the event index, and a lifted contact's point slot is never reused.
- Apply the following guards on Core's UI thread. Ignored records must not change capture, acceptance, contact state, fallback state, or the expected event index:

  | Incoming record | Core behavior |
  | --- | --- |
  | Started while idle, with a fresh sequence ID for this connection | Establish the sequence and query local acceptance exactly once. |
  | Started reusing an already-finished sequence ID in this connection | Ignore it; it cannot reopen that occurrence. |
  | Started while another sequence is active | Ignore it, retaining the original sequence. |
  | Action or End without an active matching sequence, or from an old connection | Ignore it. |
  | Action or End with an already-consumed index | Ignore it without duplicate delivery. |
  | Action with the next expected index | Deliver through the latched point/fallback path, then advance the index. |
  | Matching End with the next expected index | End once and release sequence state after callbacks. |
  | Matching action or End with a forward index gap | Report a protocol error; never silently skip a missing transition or invent a successful Up. |

- This index policy relies on the existing ordered transport: Core's async channel preserves current-renderer FIFO order, and GacJS HTTP serializes its sends. Preserve that order through all adapters and batching. Do not add retry timers or an unbounded reorder buffer. Emit every point record without the protocol's `DropRepeat`/`DropConsecutive` annotations, and do not reuse the native renderer's single pending mouse-move slot for point updates. End must follow all preceding samples, including the final normal Up.
- Scope wire sequence IDs to the current renderer connection. Map each accepted wire Started once to a fresh Core-window lifetime sequence ID, shared with the allocator used by Core automation; preserve that local ID through every hosted/composition callback. Here, accepting the wire boundary is independent of the application's point acceptance. A replacement renderer may restart its own IDs without reusing a public Core-window ID. Preserve the contact indices and sample metadata through this mapping.
- Use canonical unsigned decimal strings in wire records for the native `vuint64_t` sequence IDs, timestamps, and optional platform frame IDs, with checked C++ conversion. Do not convert full-width wire/native values through JavaScript `number`: protocol `int` currently generates `vint`, which is also only 32 bits in Win32/WASM builds. Retain null separately from an optional value of zero. Keep timestamps as monotonic microseconds. Browser-produced timestamps start as numbers; convert them to integer microseconds and require a finite, nonnegative safe integer before decimal encoding.
- Regenerate the C++ protocol through `Metadata_UpdateProtocol`; do not edit generated schema/serializer files by hand. Import the resulting upstream schema into GacJS and run its prescribed import, code generation, build, and test steps. Both peers use the updated schema; compatibility with an older point-unaware peer is not a new negotiation feature in this step.

### Core dispatch, fallback, and lifecycle

- Keep point input and fallback state with the remote native window. Wire Started runs the existing listener acceptance query; acceptance stays fixed until End. On rejection, downstream listeners still receive the paired Started/End lifecycle but no point actions. The remote renderer's End may report its own unconditional acceptance; Core must report its locally latched answer downstream.
- `ProcessNativePointInput` currently allocates sequence/contact IDs and automatically emits Started on first Down and End on last Up. Do not feed explicit protocol boundaries through it unchanged: that would duplicate boundaries or overwrite supplied identities. Reuse/refactor the relevant typed bookkeeping and dispatch so the wire boundary is delivered once and the selected ID mapping remains consistent. Final Up updates contacts but leaves the explicit protocol occurrence active until End.
- Extract reusable typed mouse fallback from `<GacUI repo>/Source/Utilities/SharedServices/GuiSharedAutomationService.cpp`, including its cancellation cleanup. Protocol input must not be converted to automation command strings or queued a second time through the command parser; that loses sample metadata and can reorder delivery.
- Rejected input produces one left-mouse stream from the original first contact only. Secondary contacts never produce mouse buttons or become the fallback contact after the first lifts. Preserve coordinates and modifiers, normal mouse hit testing/capture, and separate physical-mouse state. Cancellation clears pressed/capture state without a successful release activation. Accepted input produces no compatibility mouse stream.
- Supply the remote window's point state to `RemoteProtocolAutomationService` in `<GacUI repo>/Source/Utilities/SharedServices/GuiSharedAutomationService_Controls.cpp`; its current point-command path lacks that state and returns Unsupported. Core and renderer automation must exercise the same application semantics. Automation keeps its existing contact-command grammar and inferred boundaries; explicit transport boundaries belong to the wire protocol.
- On renderer disconnection/replacement or remote-window destruction, terminate an active local occurrence once with an appropriate existing cancellation reason, clear point capture, fallback-owned mouse state/capture, and queued point records, and retain the window-lifetime ID allocator. Use existing channel-generation/current-renderer checks to reject stale callbacks. Cancellation preserves occupied composition slots through End, without synthetic point Ups. Renderer-side trailing native cleanup cannot start another public sequence until that canceled contact group has drained.
- Retain the existing first-hosted-window/first-composition capture for the entire sequence. Renderer coordinates are native client-relative, with contact rectangles in the same space; hosted and graphics-host conversion must still handle window movement and DPI changes without converting already-logical coordinates twice.

### Native renderer and browser acquisition

- Add native point listener forwarding to `GuiRemoteRendererSingle` in `<GacUI repo>/Source/PlatformProviders/RemoteRenderer/GuiRemoteRendererSingle.h/.cpp`, using the same connection/send guards as existing IO. Its local Started callback always accepts; it forwards every boundary/action regardless of whether the application will accept. This lets the Windows provider suppress its compatibility mouse path while Core performs fallback. Disconnect stops forwarding and clears pending state.
- Add touch Pointer Event acquisition to the stable target owned by `<GacJS repo>/Gaclib/gaclib/renderer/src/GacUIRendererImpl.ts`. Keep physical mouse, wheel, keyboard, and existing pen behavior on their existing paths. Map browser pointer IDs to monotonically assigned contact indices within one overlapping-contact sequence; the primary flag does not determine its lifetime. Leave unavailable touch orientation and platform frame identity null instead of inventing hardware metadata.
- Configure `touch-action: none` across the whole renderer surface before contact begins, as renderer behavior rather than a setting only in demo CSS. Verify nested labels, paragraphs, and raw canvases remain covered after DOM updates; existing descendants use `overflow: hidden`, which establishes scroll containers under [CSS Overflow](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-overflow-3/#overflow-properties), so a root-only style must not be assumed sufficient for every hit target. Capture contacts on the stable renderer target so movement outside the surface and replacement of rendered child nodes do not lose the stream. Convert browser client coordinates/contact rectangles to renderer-client coordinates consistently with existing sizing; do not multiply coordinates by device pixel ratio merely because a canvas uses it.
- Suppress touch-origin compatibility input locally and synchronously, while preserving real mouse and non-touch activation. Cancelable touch `pointerdown` needs a non-passive listener; canceling it does not by itself suppress `click`, `auxclick`, `contextmenu`, or mouse boundary events. Correlate those separately where they would duplicate application input or trigger unwanted browser defaults. A normal Up/Cancel implicitly releases capture, so its subsequent `lostpointercapture` must not produce another End. Unexpected capture loss while active cancels the sequence. These distinctions follow the [Pointer Events specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/pointerevents3/).
- Handle `pointercancel`, renderer disposal, and capture loss using the existing cancellation reasons and one terminal notification. Drain remaining contact cleanup after a sequence-wide cancellation. Do not wait for an Up that the platform will not send, restart from a trailing move, or synthesize a successful Up. Keep one-contact and multi-contact ordering identical through the HTTP and shared worker adapters.

## No.1 [CONFIRMED] Carry explicit point boundaries through the existing ordered protocol and share typed dispatch/fallback

The current protocol schema has no point events; the native renderer has no point listener overrides. Core automation calls the shared command executor without window point state, which rejects point commands. Add generated wire records with decimal unsigned identities and explicit indices. Core owns connection-scoped guards, local sequence allocation, contact bookkeeping, acceptance, and mouse fallback. Reuse native listener dispatch and the existing fallback path without parsing synthetic automation commands. Native and browser renderers own the complete touch surface and forward ordered samples. Extend the existing Touching painters and ordinary protocol tests, then verify transport integrations and distribute self-contained guidance.

### CODE CHANGE

Native and browser raw attachments now paint the existing Touching state. Browser acquisition captures the stable target, covers descendant touch-action, preserves coalesced samples, drains cancellation, and suppresses compatibility input. Connected disposal sends one WindowDestroyed End before client teardown; disconnected cleanup stays silent. Page/session teardown ordering and its existing tests are updated accordingly.
